live_divergence_note.universe: Live scans the dynamic RS-ranked universe (universe.py, top_n=8, weekly rebalance), NOT the 12 tickers in frozen.tickers. Those 12 are the OOS validation universe only. Chosen deliberately; universe_backtest.py measures the rule point-in-time.
live_divergence_note.atr_stop: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02. The 2026-08-28 entry said 'Live now matches frozen.atr_stop=1.25' — that was true of scanner.py (which reads signal_core.DEFAULTS) but NOT of app.py, whose sidebar default was still a hardcoded 1.0. So the app showed stops, R:R and pass/fail on a value the harness never tested, while the scanner used 1.25. Two other sidebar literals had drifted the same way: hq_min_rr app 1.5 vs core 1.0 (the scanner Telegrams high-quality at 1.0) and volume_mult app 1.0 vs core 1.2 (different 'Strong' tag, which feeds high_quality). All three are now sourced from signal_core.DEFAULTS in app.py rather than written as literals, and consistency_check.py fails CI if any of them becomes a literal again. Verified: app._signal_params() == signal_core.DEFAULTS.
live_divergence_note.why_this_note: The atr_stop discrepancy went unnoticed because nothing recorded which value was chosen or why. Anything that diverges from frozen{} belongs here, dated. NOTE the 2026-08-28 entry was itself incomplete — it checked one of the two live surfaces and declared the drift closed. A note is only as good as the surfaces it actually checked; say which ones.
live_divergence_note.open_divergences_2026_09_02:
RESOLVED 2026-09-02 (regime): app.py gated the SPY regime on ADX>=20 and returned 'Neutral' below it, which signal_core reads as 'no view' — so in choppy tape the app applied NO regime filter while scanner.py still blocked counter-regime setups. backtest.build_regime_series() has no ADX gate and the 591-trade OOS ran use_regime=True, so the ungated 2-state rule is the validated one. Both callers now delegate to market_context.py; consistency_check.py asserts live regime == build_regime_series() and that ADX is reported, not gating. NOTE this makes the app STRICTER than before: it will now block counter-regime setups it used to allow through.

STILL OPEN (weekly): backtest.build_signal_params() forces weekly_confirm=False, so the OOS test validated NEITHER weekly rule. app.py used an EMA10w/EMA20w crossover and scanner.py used price vs EMA20w — opposite verdicts on ordinary pullbacks, on a BLOCKING filter. Both now use price vs EMA20w, chosen for CONSISTENCY with every other trend test in the system (daily: price>EMA20>EMA50; regime: price vs 200-SMA), NOT because it was measured. The filter itself remains unvalidated and defaults ON live, so the live config still differs from the validated one. Either add weekly bars to backtest.py and measure it, or set weekly_confirm=False to match what was actually tested.

STILL OPEN (adjustment): backtest.py fetches auto_adjust=True while every live path uses False, so the OOS result was measured on a differently-adjusted price series than live signals fire on.

WEEKLY MEASUREMENT VOID (2026-09-02): the first --use-weekly A/B (592 trades OFF vs 593 ON, -0.016R vs -0.018R) measured NOTHING. backtest.evaluate_signal() read filters['ADX Trend Strength'] and filters['Macro Regime'] but never filters['Multi-TF Alignment'], and signal_core.evaluate() does not block on any of its four enhancement filters by itself — so both arms ran an identical signal and the one-trade difference was Yahoo data drift between the two runs, not the filter. Proven offline: with weekly_confirm=True and weekly_trend=None (which must block EVERY bar) evaluate_signal still returned all 20 signals on a synthetic series. Fixed, with a falsified selftest guard in backtest.py. The A/B must be re-run before any conclusion about weekly_confirm is drawn.

WEEKLY RESOLVED (2026-09-02): re-run after the gate fix, over 15y x 12 tickers, the weekly filter rejected 5 of the 13,748 bars that reached the filters (0.04%) and 0 that no other gate would have stopped — it is evaluated after ADX>=35, and a name that trending is essentially never on the wrong side of its 20w EMA. Expectancy moved -0.016R -> -0.018R, well inside the +/-0.11 OOS CI, and inside the data feed's own run-to-run noise: two runs of the IDENTICAL command four minutes apart differed by 7 trades and 0.014R because Yahoo returned different history. Against that near-zero contribution the filter FAILS CLOSED (missing weekly trend blocks), so every rate-limited fetch was an alert outage. signal_core.DEFAULTS now has weekly_confirm=False, so live matches the config this OOS run validated. app.py still exposes it as a checkbox; scanner.py skips the weekly fetch entirely when it is off.

ADJUSTMENT RESOLVED (2026-09-02): backtest.py fetched auto_adjust=True while every live path fetched False, so the OOS result was measured on a differently-adjusted series from the one live signals fire on. Both arms were run and then REFETCHED twelve minutes later to test stability: adjusted -0.018R/593 trades but 8 of 13 series rewrote 2337-2893 rows of history on the refetch; raw -0.021R/585 trades with ZERO rows rewritten and a byte-identical fingerprint. Performance is a tie (0.003R, far inside the +/-0.11 CI); reproducibility is not. The risk that argued for adjusted bars does not exist: NFLX split 7:1 in 2015 inside this window and its raw and adjusted results are identical to the decimal, as are AMD's and ADBE's — auto_adjust=False output is ALREADY split-adjusted and only drops the dividend adjustment. backtest.py now defaults to auto_adjust=False; consistency_check.py asserts backtest and the live paths agree. IMPORTANT: the 591-trade OOS result in this lock was measured on ADJUSTED prices and is therefore NOT directly comparable to runs after this change. FROZEN's hash does not include the adjustment mode, so it did not move — re-run the OOS on the same 12 tickers (already spent, so it costs no research capital) if a comparable baseline is wanted.
